senses.sense_definition: The state of being in accordance with nature or existing in a natural state.

examples.text: The artist aimed for a sense of <w>naturalism</w> in his paintings by using only soft light and earthy colors.
The garden was designed to preserve the <w>naturalism</w> of the surrounding forest landscape.

senses.sense_definition: A style of art, literature, or theater that attempts to represent subjects as they appear in everyday life without idealization.

examples.text: The play is a classic example of <w>naturalism</w>, focusing on the gritty details of working-class life.
Many critics praised the <w>naturalism</w> of the film, noting how realistic the dialogue felt.

senses.sense_definition: The practice of living without clothes in social settings.

examples.text: Some people choose to practice <w>naturalism</w> at private beaches to feel more connected to their environment.
The resort is well-known for its commitment to <w>naturalism</w> and provides a safe space for its members.

senses.sense_definition: The philosophical belief that everything arises from natural properties and causes, excluding supernatural or spiritual explanations.

examples.text: His scientific worldview is rooted in <w>naturalism</w>, as he rejects any claims of divine intervention.
The debate between religious faith and <w>naturalism</w> has been a central theme in modern philosophy.

senses.sense_definition: A philosophical system that views nature as governed by fixed laws without the direction of a conscious will.

examples.text: The theory relies on <w>naturalism</w> to explain the evolution of complex systems through blind physical forces.
By adopting <w>naturalism</w>, the researchers focused entirely on observable physical phenomena.

senses.sense_definition: The view that there is no fundamental difference between scientific and philosophical methods of inquiry.

examples.text: Methodological <w>naturalism</w> suggests that philosophy should be continuous with the empirical sciences.
The professor argued that <w>naturalism</w> is the most effective framework for modern epistemological research.

senses.sense_definition: The belief that there are universal moral or legal principles inherent in nature.

examples.text: Legal <w>naturalism</w> posits that human laws must be based on objective moral truths found in nature.
The philosopher defended <w>naturalism</w> by arguing that justice is a fundamental aspect of the natural order.
